headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default; Langflow’s unsandboxed Python and server-side state amplify the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra reads/writes files and emits workflow outputs; Langflow ingests flow inputs and intermediate outputs, with server-side state and stores. That creates a plausible file-based or output-based bridge where attacker-controlled content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. No shared MCP is shown, so medium is the higher justified level.
conditions: IF Kestra writes untrusted content into /app/storage or /tmp and Langflow later reads it as flow input
IF Langflow chains a node that interprets Kestra-produced text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different hosts or containers
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files between the two systems
Add provenance tags and reject untrusted instruction-like content
Use read-only mounts for any shared directory
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing at the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while Langflow handles flow inputs, intermediate outputs, uploaded files, and stored credentials. Both have broad network egress and filesystem access, so sensitive data can flow from Kestra into Langflow and then out through model providers or HTTP services. The default blast radius includes exfiltration and compliance breach.
conditions: IF Kestra workflows pass logs, database data, or cloud storage data into Langflow flows
IF Langflow components send those inputs to external model providers or arbitrary HTTP services
mitigations: Do not pass sensitive datasets between the agents
Restrict Langflow flows to local-only providers and endpoints
Redact logs and payloads before any handoff
Place both agents behind an egress allowlist
requires-engineering: enforce data-class policies at the workflow boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and Kestra also requests root/docker.sock while Langflow runs Python code server-side by default. Even without modify_git_state on Langflow, overlapping unrestricted writes to shared paths plus privileged execution creates a strong conflict risk if they operate on the same workspace or deployment. Uncertainty about deployment isolation pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same writable directory or volume
IF Kestra uses root or docker.sock while Langflow executes Python code on the same host
mitigations: Run the agents in separate containers with separate volumes
Remove root and docker.sock from Kestra unless strictly required
Disable or isolate Langflow Python code components
Use per-agent service accounts and distinct working directories
requires-engineering: add locking or transactional coordination on shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is explicitly a graph-based flow system that can chain multiple agents, and Kestra produces workflow outputs, logs, and notifications. If Langflow consumes Kestra output as authoritative input, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions without verification. Because both have action-taking surfaces and broad egress, the default risk is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF Langflow uses Kestra-generated text as a node input without validation
IF a Langflow flow triggers external API calls or agent actions based on Kestra output
mitigations: Insert a human review step before downstream actions
Require schema validation on Kestra outputs before Langflow consumes them
Mark Kestra outputs as untrusted in the flow metadata
Limit Langflow nodes that can trigger side effects
requires-engineering: add verification gates and typed contracts between systems

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra touches database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while Langflow stores per-flow credentials and processes uploaded files and intermediate outputs. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, but the shared handling of sensitive operational data plus stored secrets creates a plausible retention and subject-rights mismatch. Uncertainty prevents a lower rating.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Kestra workflows into Langflow flows
IF Langflow retains uploaded files or intermediate outputs longer than Kestra’s retention policy
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data into the pair
Align retention settings across both systems
Document deletion and export procedures for shared data classes
Restrict Langflow secret storage to non-regulated credentials
requires-engineering: perform a residency and certification review before deployment
